verdict.rationale: Lium has no built-in natural-language interface. It does ship first-party agent-facing pieces: an MCP server that lets an AI client search the docs and query live GPU prices and availability, and an agent skill (SKILL.md) for agents that can 'do everything on Lium with no browser'. However, the MCP tools are read-only (docs, prices, rent links), and actually renting or removing pods depends on the user's own agent driving the CLI or API. missing for 10: a first-party natural-language command interface, MCP tools that perform operations (rent/exec/remove) rather than only read docs and prices, and independent hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Use the MCP server at `/mcp` to search and read the docs (`search`, `read_page`) and to see live GPU prices and availability with rent links (`search_gpus`, `get_gpu_prices`).
Your agent starts a pod, runs the job and removes it, within a budget you set.
An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
